this_host_does_not_send: This host does not send hardware info.
tap_a_name_to_show: Tap a name to show/hide it
tap_a_name_above_to: Tap a name above to show its line
speaker: Speaker
sound_not_supported_on_this: Sound: not supported on this board
no_battery_on_this_deck: No battery on this Deck's input
do_not_power_off: Do not power off: the Deck restarts by itself
help_monitor:
The PC's live values, sent by the host.
Tap a bar or a box to open that component: its values, its hardware and its history.

PC MONITOR and CONTROLS at the bottom switch pages.

Top: the dot and USB / WI-FI show the link to the host (green connected, amber lost, grey never seen); the gear opens Settings, a tap on the clock shows the date. The battery shows when one is connected.
help_macros:
Six keys that run actions on the PC. The actions are set in the host's settings.

A tap runs the key's action and the key flashes.

While OpenDeck runs with the Control Deck plugin, the keys show OpenDeck's images and run its actions instead.

Nothing runs without a host connected.
help_detail:
This component's values now, and its hardware as the host reports it. N/A: the host has no measurement for it.

Bars: usage and temperatures from 0 to 100. Network and disk rates: relative to the highest value seen since power-on.

HISTORY opens the graph of the last minutes.
help_history:
One line per value of this component, from the record the host keeps.
Tap a name above the graph to show or hide its line; it also shows the newest value.
Same units, or % with degrees, share the axis; otherwise each line has its own scale and the axis no numbers.
5m to 20m: the period. A gap: no measurement then.
help_connectivity:
How the Deck reaches the host.
Wi-Fi: saved networks. Bluetooth: BLE and pairing. Host: address, port, token.
USE WI-FI / USE USB: the link to use. Wi-Fi needs the host's address and token, given over USB: connect the cable once.
SCREEN: brightness, screen off, rotation. SOUND: speaker, microphone.
Host in, Loop: counters for finding faults.
help_wifi_profiles:
The saved Wi-Fi networks, at most 5. The Deck tries the enabled ones, the preferred first.

Tap a network to connect to it, make it preferred, change its password, move it or delete it.

SCAN / ADD: look for networks in range and add one.
help_wifi_profile:
One saved network.

CONNECT / DISCONNECT. SET PREFERRED: tried first. DISABLE: not tried by itself. PASSWORD: change it. MOVE UP / DOWN: the order the networks are tried in.

DELETE asks for a second tap.

While connected, the page shows what the network gave the Deck: address, mask, gateway, DNS, MAC and channel.
help_wifi_scan:
The networks the Deck can see. Tap one to add it; its password is asked next.

+ Add by name: a hidden network, or one out of range now.

UP / DOWN scroll the list. RESCAN looks again (STOP while it looks).
help_keyboard:
Type the text named in the title.

SHIFT: one capital letter. #+=: digits and symbols, ABC: back to letters. DEL: deletes the last character. The eye in a password field shows or hides it.

OK keeps the text, CANCEL leaves it as it was. Bottom right: length and limit.
help_wifi_host:
Where the host is: its address, port and token. Over USB the host gives them to the Deck by itself.

Tap a line to type it.

FIND: looks for hosts on this network (private networks only; the PC's firewall must let UDP 8080 in).

TEST: checks the address and the token.
help_sound:
Speaker ON: a click on each tap. Volume: - and + play a beep at the new volume.
Microphone ON: its level shows in the bar below. Gain: how loud it hears.
TEST SPK: three notes from the speaker. TEST MIC: records 3 s (speak), then plays back what it heard.
Kept when you leave the page. Later: talking to the PC (speech to text, text to speech) through them.
help_ble:
Bluetooth LE as the link to the host, in place of the cable.
USE BLE: the Deck shows itself to the PC. Pair once from the PC's Bluetooth settings, typing the 6-digit code this page then shows; after that the PC connects by itself.
Below: the PCs paired with this Deck, the preferred one first, green when connected. Tap one to disconnect it, prefer it, disable, rename or forget it. USE USB: back to the cable.
help_screen:
Brightness: - and + in steps of 10%. A dimmer screen makes the battery last longer.
Screen off: after this long without a tap the screen dims, 10 s later it goes dark and the CPU slows down; the Deck stays connected. The first tap only lights it.
Rotation: each tap turns the screen a quarter turn further (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees). The new pages follow every turn; an older page that does not fit a portrait screen stays in landscape until it is redone.
All three are kept when you leave the page.
help_battery:
The battery input of the board: its voltage now, the lowest and highest since power-on, how fast it changes and the last 30 minutes.
The board measures only the voltage. Charge and time left are estimates for a one-cell LiPo on the board's battery connector; under load it reads lower.
Power: battery, USB while it charges, or USB with the battery full or none. Only a computer on the port is seen: a charger or power bank looks like battery.
help_host_list: More than one host answered on this network. Tap the one this Deck should use: its address is saved and tested.
help_settings:
Everything the Deck lets you change, from the gear on every page.
Connection: USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the host. Screen: brightness, screen off, rotation. Sound: speaker and microphone, or not supported on this board.
Touch: the controller as it answers now; a resistive one is recalibrated with two taps (the Deck restarts). Power: the battery. About: the chip, its flash and the free memory.
Firmware: a tap asks the server for a newer one; a second tap installs it over Wi-Fi (the Deck restarts with it).
help_inbox:
The messages the server left for this Deck, the newest first; a dot marks those not read yet. Tap one to read it (or hear it): the server learns it was read.
RECORD leaves a voice message for the people at the PC.
Messages are left on the PC (the server's POST /api/messages). The gear shows how many are unread.
help_message: One message: who left it, how long ago, and its text. A voice message: PLAY fetches its audio from the server and plays it. BACK returns to the list.
help_ble_pc:
One PC paired with this Deck, by its Bluetooth address.
DISCONNECT: drops the link now (the PC may connect again). SET PREFERRED: listed first. DISABLE: the PC is sent away each time it connects, until enabled again. RENAME: the name on the Deck only.
FORGET THIS PC (two taps): removes the pairing; the PC must pair again, and should forget the Deck too.
help_record:
A voice message for the people at the PC, up to 30 s.
RECORD starts, STOP ends it; PLAY hears it again; SEND gives it to the server, which keeps it with the messages (on the PC: GET /api/messages/<id>/audio).
A new RECORD replaces it.
help_about:
The chip, its flash and memory, the Deck's id, the firmware, how long it has been running and why it last started.
RESTART (two taps) starts the Deck again; nothing is lost.
help_touch:
The touch controller as it answers now, and the last point touched (raw and on the screen).
RECALIBRATE (two taps) restarts the Deck into the calibration: tap each target as it shows.
